jobs.title: GIS-Remote sensing-QA
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a GIS-Remote Sensing-QA based in India.

This role offers an opportunity to work at the intersection of GIS, remote sensing, imagery interpretation, and geospatial quality assurance.

You’ll analyze high-resolution satellite and aerial imagery to identify physical features and detect changes across different time periods.

Your work will help ensure spatial datasets are accurate, complete, consistent, and reliable for downstream project use.

You’ll combine visual interpretation with digitization, spatial analysis, validation, and structured quality-control processes.

The role involves working with tools such as QGIS and ArcGIS and managing a range of common geospatial data formats.

You’ll collaborate with project teams to document findings, communicate discrepancies, and produce clear maps and analytical outputs.

This is a strong opportunity for an experienced geospatial professional to contribute to data-driven mapping and analysis projects with real-world impact.

Accountabilities

Interpret high-resolution satellite and aerial imagery to identify, classify, and assess physical features and changes within the built environment.
Compare imagery captured at different dates to identify spatial changes and document observations accurately and consistently.
Validate interpreted features against reference datasets, identify discrepancies, and record uncertainty where applicable.
Digitize, update, and maintain spatial features and associated attributes using QGIS and/or ArcGIS.
Assess imagery suitability for analysis by considering spatial resolution, acquisition date, cloud cover, shadows, and other image-quality factors.
Perform detailed geospatial QA/QC checks to verify the accuracy, completeness, consistency, and reliability of project deliverables.
Prepare, validate, and manage datasets in formats such as SHP, KML/KMZ, GeoJSON, and GeoTIFF.
Document analytical methods, observations, quality findings, and project outcomes in a clear and structured manner.
Create maps and concise analytical summaries to communicate findings effectively to project stakeholders.
Support project teams in resolving data discrepancies and maintaining consistent geospatial interpretation standards.

Requirements

4–5 years of professional experience in GIS, remote sensing, satellite imagery interpretation, or a closely related field.
Hands-on experience working with high-resolution satellite and/or aerial imagery.
Strong visual interpretation skills, including the ability to recognize built features, land disturbance, surface characteristics, and changes over time.
Experience with multi-temporal imagery comparison, change detection, feature validation, and reference-data analysis.
Proficiency with QGIS and/or ArcGIS for visualization, digitization, spatial analysis, and geospatial data management.
Strong understanding of imagery quality factors, including resolution, acquisition timing, cloud cover, shadows, and their impact on interpretation confidence.
Practical experience performing geospatial quality assurance and quality control.
Familiarity with SHP, KML/KMZ, GeoJSON, GeoTIFF, and other commonly used GIS data formats.
Strong attention to detail and the ability to identify subtle inconsistencies or spatial discrepancies.
Good analytical, organizational, documentation, and communication skills.
Ability to work independently while maintaining consistent quality standards and project timelines.
Experience interpreting urban imagery or mapping the built environment is preferred.
Familiarity with commercial high-resolution satellite imagery providers or imagery platforms is an advantage.
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Geography, Geoinformatics, Remote Sensing, Civil Engineering, Urban Planning, or a related discipline.

Benefits

Full-time consultant/freelancer opportunity based in India.
Onsite or hybrid working arrangement, depending on project requirements.
Opportunity to work extensively with high-resolution satellite and aerial imagery.
Hands-on experience across GIS, remote sensing, geospatial analysis, and quality assurance.
Opportunity to contribute to projects involving urban mapping, built-environment analysis, and change detection.
Exposure to widely used GIS tools and industry-standard geospatial data formats.
Collaborative environment with opportunities to support project teams and contribute to high-quality geospatial deliverables.
Professional opportunity to further develop expertise in GIS, remote sensing, imagery analysis, and geospatial QA/QC.

jobs.description:
Wendel, an Esri Business Partner and multi‑disciplinary Architectural and Engineering firm, is seeking an experienced part‑time, provisional GIS Analyst for a short‑term engagement. The position will be based out of the Williamsville, New York office, with flexibility for candidates located near other Wendel office locations. This role is focused on ArcGIS Enterprise administration, spatial web services, and cloud-hosted GIS solutions supporting companywide projects across multiple disciplines. The analyst will collaborate directly with the GIS Manager, Developers, and Project Managers to deliver enterprise-level geospatial infrastructure and analyses.

Responsibilities

Administer ArcGIS Enterprise (Portal for ArcGIS, Data Store) within virtualized server environments
Publish, manage, and maintain hosted feature layers through ArcGIS Enterprise Portal, ensuring performance and availability of REST service endpoints.
Build and maintain web mapping applications using ArcGIS Experience Builder, Web AppBuilder, etc.
Convert and integrate GIS data to/from CAD formats and perform advanced spatial analysis (buffering, overlays, network analysis, distance calculations).
Manage mobile field data collection workflows using ArcGIS Field Maps and Survey123, including form design and data synchronization with enterprise hosted layers.
Support the GIS Developer with SQL database administration to automate workflows
Conduct client training on web applications, GPS collection, and enterprise GIS workflows for internal and external stakeholders

Qualifications

B.A. or B.S. in Geography, GIS, or related field.
3+ years of professional GIS experience.
Demonstrated ArcGIS Enterprise administration experience (Portal, Server, Data Store).
Experience working with GIS infrastructure in virtualized server environments
Proficient in Esri's full ArcGIS suite including ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, and Enterprise Portal.
Experience publishing and managing REST services (map, feature, image, and geoprocessing)
Strong working knowledge of SDE geodatabases
Proficient in Python scripting with ArcPy for automation of publishing workflows, data processing, and geodatabase management.
Strong understanding of REST API architecture and experience troubleshooting service endpoints.
Experience with coordinate systems, projections, and spatial reference management at an enterprise scale.
Experience with mobile data collection platforms: ArcGIS Survey123 and ArcGIS Field Maps.
Demonstrated ability to produce publication-quality maps, figures, and visuals for project deliverables.
Strong analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills with the ability to work independently and on a team.

Hourly Range: $32.21 - $59.13

Wendel is committed to providing fair, competitive, and market-informed compensation. The rate offered will be determined based off the successful candidates’ relevant education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities. jobs.description:
About the opportunity
Have you developed or maintained a C#/ASP.NET application that integrates with Esri ArcGIS and an Oracle enterprise geodatabase? We would like to hear from you.

Imperious Enterprise LLC is assembling a small team for a proposed three-year application-support engagement with an Ohio public-sector utility. We are seeking a senior developer to maintain and enhance an existing stormwater billing application that connects customer accounts, parcel information, GIS data, and billing workflows. ( We have a strong preference for people in Ohio)

Our priority is hands-on application-development experience across .NET, ArcGIS, and Oracle not GIS mapping experience alone.
This role involves understanding an established codebase, troubleshooting issues, and delivering reliable improvements rather than building a replacement system.
Independent consultants and small specialist firms are welcome.

The experience that matters most
We are looking for demonstrated experience in three core areas:
C#/ASP.NET MVC application development:
Maintaining existing applications, debugging backend and user-interface issues, implementing enhancements, and testing changes.
Esri ArcGIS integration:
Developing applications or automated workflows that interact with ArcGIS services, parcel data, and enterprise geodatabases.
Oracle databases and geodatabases:
Writing SQL, troubleshooting data issues, modifying application schemas, and supporting workflows connecting application and GIS data.

Experience using these technologies together in a production application
is especially valuable. Supporting skills should include Python, JavaScript, batch-processing troubleshooting, Git/GitHub, and basic Windows Server and deployment networking knowledge.
Utility billing, stormwater, municipal GIS, and public-sector experience are preferred. Comparable enterprise application maintenance and integration experience is also relevant.
What you will do
Maintain and enhance the application’s C#/ASP.NET code, Oracle data workflows, and ArcGIS integrations.
Investigate batch failures, data-quality issues, and application defects escalated by the client’s IT team.
Develop and test fixes, enhancements, and database changes; contribute to a planned .NET upgrade.
Participate in GitHub code reviews, document changes, and support user acceptance testing and technical knowledge transfer.

You will work with an assigned project manager and the client’s IT, GIS, and billing staff. The client’s IT team handles production deployments, rollbacks, and post-release checks.

Engagement and availability
This is a part-time support engagement
, with scheduled development work and on-demand troubleshooting not a full-time assignment. Hours and compensation will be agreed before engagement.
Availability at the beginning of the client’s Eastern Time business day is important for urgent batch issues. Occasional weekend emergency assistance may be needed, with coverage arrangements agreed in advance. Plan for at least one annual on-site visit to Cleveland, Ohio; most collaboration will be remote.
The position is contingent on contract award.

Compensation:
$90–$110/hour, depending on demonstrated C#/ASP.NET, Oracle, and Esri ArcGIS/geodatabase experience. Part-time contract opportunity, contingent on award. Hours, support coverage, and travel arrangements will be agreed before engagement.

By integrating advisory services with over 30 technical environmental and engineering disciplines, we help clients navigate complex environmental challenges and advance their sustainability goals.

At SLR, our work supports better environmental outcomes for communities, ecosystems, and industry. Together with our clients, we are committed to Making Sustainability Happen.

As our newest Environmental Risk Assessor
, you will play an important role in supporting this mission.

Working within our national Risk Assessment team, you will contribute to a variety of complex environmental projects while applying your regulatory knowledge and continuing to expand your expertise in provincial and federal requirements. In this role, you will collaborate closely with internal teams, clients, and regulators to develop technical scopes of work, prepare proposals, and support the successful management and delivery of projects.

This role offers exceptional opportunities for professional growth, providing the chance to work on projects from coast to coast and collaborate with experienced teams across North America, all while gaining exposure to a wide range of regulatory frameworks, environmental challenges, and consulting practices. Working on complex, multidisciplinary projects across sectors such as mining, oil and gas, land development, and federal, provincial, territorial, and municipal jurisdictions will allow you to continually deepen your technical expertise. You’ll also gain valuable experience navigating emerging contaminants and engaging with diverse stakeholders, including regulators, Indigenous communities, industry partners, and the general public. This variety will not only strengthen your technical foundation, but accelerate your development as a well‑rounded environmental professional capable of leading in dynamic and evolving practice areas.

Our team is passionate about delivering high-quality work and building strong client relationships. We are looking for someone who shares this mindset and brings strong communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage competing priorities in a dynamic consulting environment. Success in this role will require flexibility, independence, and a commitment to delivering high-quality technical work.

Specific Responsibilities Will Include

Develop and deliver human health and ecological risk assessments, risk management plans, performance verification plans, etc. in accordance with provincial, territorial, and federal regulatory frameworks

Evaluate site-specific physical characteristics, environmental data, receptor exposure assumptions, and toxicity information to inform the development of exposure and risk models.

Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to prepare high-quality technical reports and effectively communicate findings to clients, regulators, and other stakeholders.

Salary range: $75,000 – $115,000 Final agreed upon compensation will reflect education, professional designation, experience, internal parity, and location

jobs.title: Professional Biologist / Project Wildlife Biologist Lead
jobs.description:
About Us

TRC, Member of WSP, is a global consulting environmental and engineering firm and one of the top design firms in the energy sector. Together, TRC and WSP’s 83,000 experts create positive, long-lasting impacts for our communities and our clients in the power and energy, transportation and infrastructure, environmental, and property and buildings sectors. As part of our team, you’ll discover a world of opportunities to connect with innovative thinkers, forge your path, and have fun tackling the world’s most challenging projects. At TRC, Member of WSP, you can have a rewarding career on every level.

TRC has long set the bar for clients who require more than just engineering, combining science with the latest technology to devise innovative solutions that stand the test of time. From pipelines to power plants, roadways to reservoirs, schoolyards to security solutions, clients look to TRC for breakthrough thinking backed by the innovative follow-through of an industry leader.

We recognize that the expertise of our staff is our strongest asset, so we generously reward employees for successful performance and invest in their careers through training and the development of new skills and certifications.

Overview

TRC is seeking a Experienced Professional Biologist/Project Wildlife Biologist Lead to join its successful Planning, Permitting, and Licensing practice in Colorado or surrounding states. This position requires an interdisciplinary, technical, and regulatory specialist who will provide technical leadership for public and private sector clients regarding wildlife specific issues. Typical work would include conducting field surveys, completing survey reports, completing and reviewing wildlife sections for federal, state and local permitting for clients. The successful candidate will be entrusted with managing and leading field studies for projects, conducting and reporting studies related to their technical discipline to meet regulatory requirements, and preparing documents supporting permitting processes.

The successful individual will have significant experience working on conducting, leading, and coordinating a full range of biological field surveys and completing the associated reporting. A successful candidate will have demonstrated experience with surveys of regional migratory birds, including eagles and other raptors. Experience with other typical regional wildlife species such as grouse species, bats, small mammals, desert tortoise, and other wildlife if preferred. This individual should demonstrate experience leading and managing field work scopes for projects associated with transportation and/or energy projects and should have the ability to guide the agencies and TRC’s project partners through the environmental processes to meet applicable wildlife laws and regulations to successfully achieve project design goals.

Responsibilities

Conduct biological field surveys which may include habitat, or wildlife and plant species-specific surveys, conduct breeding bird and raptor surveys, greater sage-grouse lek counts, small mammal trapping, and wetland/waterbody delineations (in accordance with USACE requirements).
Provide environmental planning expertise pertaining to National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) as implemented by federal agencies such as the Bureau of Land Management (BLM), United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), United States Forest Service (USFS), United States Fish and Wildlife Service (USFW), the Department of Energy (DOE), Department of the Interior (DOI), Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), Western Area/Bonneville Power Administration, Federal Transit Administration (FTA), Federal Railroad Administration (FRA), Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), and respective requirements/regulations.
Engage as a client-facing technical leader with in-depth knowledge pertaining to the planning of renewables, Oil & Gas, transportation, mining, and/or other industrial projects and advancing such projects through the local, state and federal government approval process. Interact directly with the agencies/clients as TRC’s environmental planning subject matter expert.
Demonstrated experience with State and Local permitting in one or more of the following states AZ, CO, ID, KS, NE, ND, NM, NV, MT, OR, SD, UT, WA, and WY.
Prepare desktop critical issues analysis reports.
Prepare technical reports from field surveys such as wetland reports and threatened and endangered species habitat reports.
Prepare agency consultation letters to agencies such as USFWS and State Wildlife and Fisheries.
Support marketing and business development efforts and represent TRC at industry functions.
Support proposal preparation for a range of industries.
Lead and manage the preparation of project-related environmental documentation (e.g., initial studies, environmental impact statements, environmental assessments, categorical exclusions and exemptions, and negative declarations).
Mentor and train junior staff that will support the successful candidate in implementing the work.
This is a leadership role and is expected to require staff management.

Qualifications

5+ years of experience conducting field surveys involving wildlife habitat delineations, bird identification, avian nest locations, lek counts and/or monitoring, and/or small mammal trapping.
Demonstrated experience leading and managing field efforts and following survey protocols.
Possesses the ability to guide agencies/clients through the environmental processes required to meet applicable environmental compliance and permitting laws and regulations.

jobs.description:
Your job

Are you intrigued by interactions between vegetation and fire? Are you passionate about lab-, field-, and remote sensing-based research? Do you like solving scientific puzzles? We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to explore how moss traits affect fire ignitability in high-latitude ecosystems.

Northern ecosystems, including boreal peatlands and tundra, are warming faster than almost anywhere else on Earth, which is changing their structure and functioning. Permafrost thaw and increasing fire frequency threaten to turn these ecosystems from carbon sinks into carbon, further accelerating climate change. Bryophytes (including mosses) dominate the vegetation across much of these carbon-dense ecosystems. Because of their unique water-retention and insulating properties, they largely determine how susceptible these regions are to severe wildfires. This PhD project
examines the relationship between bryophyte functional traits and fire dynamics at the plant, ecosystem, and biome scales, combining lab experiments, fieldwork, and remote sensing. Building on the PEN research line on vegetation-climate feedbacks, your work will advance our understanding of the functional role of bryophytes in fire dynamics and help improve fire risk assessments for these vulnerable systems.

Your Duties And Responsibilities Include

Developing methods and designing and executing experiments to test moss ignitability
Conducting fieldwork in high-latitude ecosystems, including vegetation surveys, monitoring environmental conditions during and after fires, and possibly drone-based observations
Analysing remote sensing data and global vegetation databases
Publishing your research in peer-reviewed journals and presenting it at national and international conferences
Co-supervising BSc and MSc students

Position Title: Director of Environmental

Function / Department: Environment, Health, Safety & Sustainability (EHS&S)

Location / Base: Gramercy, Louisiana (primary), with recurring on-site presence in St. Ann, Jamaica

Travel: Approximately 20–35%, including regular international travel to Jamaica

Jurisdictions United States (Federal / State of Louisiana) and Jamaica, with the ability to extend to other jurisdictions for potential M&A or other reasons

Position Summary

The Director of Environmental provides strategic and operational leadership for all environmental compliance, stewardship, and sustainability activities across Atalco's integrated bauxite-to-alumina value chain. The role holds single-point accountability for environmental performance at two geographically and jurisdictionally distinct operations: the Gramercy alumina refinery in Louisiana, United States, and the St. Ann bauxite mining operation in Jamaica.

Reporting to senior leadership, the Director sets environmental policy and standards, ensures full compliance with all applicable United States federal and Louisiana state regulations as well as Jamaican national environmental and mining law, and drives a proactive culture of environmental risk management, continuous improvement, and responsible resource stewardship. The role is central to protecting Atalco's license to operate, managing all permitting, exploration, alumina processing, bauxite residue and mined-land liabilities, safeguarding air, water, and land resources, and maintaining constructive relationships with regulators, communities, and other stakeholders in both countries.

Scope of Operations

Gramercy Alumina Refinery — Gramercy, Louisiana, USA

A Bayer-process alumina refinery on the Mississippi River that converts imported bauxite into smelter- and chemical-grade aluminas. Key environmental features and risk areas include Title V air emissions sources (calcination, digestion, power/steam generation), process and stormwater discharges to the Mississippi River under a Louisiana water discharge permit, bauxite residue (red mud) storage and management areas, caustic and chemical handling, spill prevention, and hazardous and industrial waste management within a densely regulated US industrial corridor. This scope is expanding to cover gallium extraction from the Gramercy Bayer process, as well as potentially the beneficiation of critical minerals and other elements from the bauxite residue.

St. Ann Bauxite Operation — St. Ann Parish, Jamaica

An open-pit bauxite mining, drying, and export operation set in Jamaica's karst limestone terrain. Key environmental features and risk areas include permitting, exploration, sensitive specie preservation and relocation, land clearing and progressive mine development, mined-land reclamation and restoration, dust and air quality management from mining, trucking, railing, and drying, material handling/conveying, ship loading, protection of groundwater and surface water resources, biodiversity and reforestation obligations, haul-road and shipping-terminal impacts, and management of overburden and red-earth materials—all governed by Jamaican environmental permits, licenses, and mining lease conditions.

Key Responsibilities

Environmental Strategy & Leadership

Define and own the environmental strategy, policy, standards, permits, and related management systems that apply consistently across both operations while respecting each jurisdiction's legal requirements.
Establish a single, harmonized environmental management framework (aligned to ISO 14001 principles) that sets a common standard of performance while accommodating US and Jamaican regulatory differences.
Serve as the company's principal environmental authority, advising the executive team and Board on environmental risk, liabilities, obligations, capital requirements, and emerging regulatory developments.
Embed environmental accountability into operational decision-making, capital planning, and site leadership performance objectives.

Regulatory Compliance — Gramercy (United States)

Ensure full and continuous compliance with all applicable US federal and Louisiana state environmental requirements, including the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA), and Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act (EPCRA).
Own the site's Title V air operating permit, Louisiana water discharge (LPDES) permit, and all related permits, ensuring conditions, monitoring, and reporting obligations are met.
Maintain compliant relationships and correspondence with the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality (LDEQ) and applicable local agencies.
Oversee Toxic Release Inventory (TRI / Form R), Tier II, greenhouse gas, and other mandated federal and state reporting.
Direct Spill Prevention, Control and Countermeasure (SPCC), stormwater, and hazardous/industrial waste programs.
Optimize management of environmental liabilities and closure related plans.

Regulatory Compliance — St. Ann (Jamaica)

Ensure full compliance with Jamaican environmental and mining legislation, including the Natural Resources Conservation Authority (NRCA) Act, environmental permits and licenses, and conditions of the Mining Act and applicable Special Mining Leases.
Maintain effective working relationships with the National Environment and Planning Agency (NEPA), the Natural Resources Conservation Authority (NRCA), the Jamaica Bauxite Institute (JBI), Mines and Geology Division / Commissioner of Mines, and applicable local agencies.
Manage environmental permit and license applications, renewals, Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs), environmental permit conditions, and related matters for mine exploration, development and expansion.
Ensure compliance with mined-land reclamation, restoration, and post-mining land-use obligations under Jamaican law and lease commitments.

Bauxite Residue, Waste & Materials Management

Direct the safe management, processing, monitoring, and long-term stewardship of bauxite residue (red mud) storage areas at Gramercy, including structural integrity, seepage control, water balance, and closure planning.
Oversee management of overburden, red-earth, tailings, and process waste materials at St. Ann in line with permit conditions and reclamation plans.
Ensure hazardous, industrial, and general waste is characterized, stored, transported, and disposed of in compliance with applicable regulations at both sites.

Air, Water, Land & Biodiversity

Oversee air emissions monitoring, control, and dust management across refining from bauxite discharging through to final product loading (Gramercy) and mining/drying/shipping (St. Ann) activities.
Manage water resources, process water, wastewater, and stormwater programs, including discharge monitoring, groundwater and surface-water protection, and water quality reporting.
Lead progressive mined-land reclamation, revegetation, reforestation, and biodiversity protection programs at St. Ann, and land stewardship and site remediation at Gramercy.

Permitting, Monitoring & Reporting

Own the full lifecycle of environmental permits, licenses, and authorizations at both operations—applications, renewals, modifications, and condition tracking.
Ensure timely, accurate, and defensible environmental monitoring, recordkeeping, and regulatory reporting in both jurisdictions.
Maintain an audit-ready compliance calendar and documentation system spanning both sites.

Incident Management & Emergency Response

Establish and maintain environmental incident prevention, spill response, and emergency preparedness programs at both operations.
Lead environmental incident investigations, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and regulatory notification and follow-up.
Ensure emergency response plans meet US and Jamaican requirements and are regularly tested and updated.

Auditing, Assurance & Continuous Improvement

Implement a program of internal and third-party environmental audits, inspections, and self-assessments across both sites.
Track environmental performance against targets, identify improvement opportunities, and drive corrective and preventive actions to closure.
Benchmark performance and adopt industry-leading practices in alumina refining and bauxite mining environmental management.

Stakeholder, Community & Sustainability Engagement

Represent Atalco with regulators, government agencies, industry bodies, and communities in both Louisiana and Jamaica.
Support community relations, land-use, and social-license initiatives associated with mining and refining operations.
Advance Atalco's sustainability, ESG, and greenhouse-gas / decarbonization reporting and commitments.

Team Leadership & Resources

Lead, develop, and mentor site environmental teams at Gramercy and St. Ann, building bench strength and consistent standards across borders.
Develop and manage the environmental function's operating and capital budgets, including compliance, monitoring, remediation, and reclamation expenditures.
Manage environmental consultants, laboratories, and specialist contractors in both jurisdictions.
Identify and develop succession candidates for environmental managers at both locations and other key environmental roles.

Your job

Are you intrigued by interactions between vegetation and fire? Are you passionate about lab-, field-, and remote sensing-based research? Do you like solving scientific puzzles? We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to explore how moss traits affect fire ignitability in high-latitude ecosystems.

Northern ecosystems, including boreal peatlands and tundra, are warming faster than almost anywhere else on Earth, which is changing their structure and functioning. Permafrost thaw and increasing fire frequency threaten to turn these ecosystems from carbon sinks into carbon, further accelerating climate change. Bryophytes (including mosses) dominate the vegetation across much of these carbon-dense ecosystems. Because of their unique water-retention and insulating properties, they largely determine how susceptible these regions are to severe wildfires. This PhD project
examines the relationship between bryophyte functional traits and fire dynamics at the plant, ecosystem, and biome scales, combining lab experiments, fieldwork, and remote sensing. Building on the PEN research line on vegetation-climate feedbacks, your work will advance our understanding of the functional role of bryophytes in fire dynamics and help improve fire risk assessments for these vulnerable systems.

Your Duties And Responsibilities Include

Developing methods and designing and executing experiments to test moss ignitability
Conducting fieldwork in high-latitude ecosystems, including vegetation surveys, monitoring environmental conditions during and after fires, and possibly drone-based observations
Analysing remote sensing data and global vegetation databases
Publishing your research in peer-reviewed journals and presenting it at national and international conferences
Co-supervising BSc and MSc students

Position Summary

The Director of Environmental provides strategic and operational leadership for all environmental compliance, stewardship, and sustainability activities across Atalco's integrated bauxite-to-alumina value chain. The role holds single-point accountability for environmental performance at two geographically and jurisdictionally distinct operations: the Gramercy alumina refinery in Louisiana, United States, and the St. Ann bauxite mining operation in Jamaica.

Reporting to senior leadership, the Director sets environmental policy and standards, ensures full compliance with all applicable United States federal and Louisiana state regulations as well as Jamaican national environmental and mining law, and drives a proactive culture of environmental risk management, continuous improvement, and responsible resource stewardship. The role is central to protecting Atalco's license to operate, managing all permitting, exploration, alumina processing, bauxite residue and mined-land liabilities, safeguarding air, water, and land resources, and maintaining constructive relationships with regulators, communities, and other stakeholders in both countries.

Scope of Operations

Gramercy Alumina Refinery — Gramercy, Louisiana, USA

A Bayer-process alumina refinery on the Mississippi River that converts imported bauxite into smelter- and chemical-grade aluminas. Key environmental features and risk areas include Title V air emissions sources (calcination, digestion, power/steam generation), process and stormwater discharges to the Mississippi River under a Louisiana water discharge permit, bauxite residue (red mud) storage and management areas, caustic and chemical handling, spill prevention, and hazardous and industrial waste management within a densely regulated US industrial corridor. This scope is expanding to cover gallium extraction from the Gramercy Bayer process, as well as potentially the beneficiation of critical minerals and other elements from the bauxite residue.

St. Ann Bauxite Operation — St. Ann Parish, Jamaica

An open-pit bauxite mining, drying, and export operation set in Jamaica's karst limestone terrain. Key environmental features and risk areas include permitting, exploration, sensitive specie preservation and relocation, land clearing and progressive mine development, mined-land reclamation and restoration, dust and air quality management from mining, trucking, railing, and drying, material handling/conveying, ship loading, protection of groundwater and surface water resources, biodiversity and reforestation obligations, haul-road and shipping-terminal impacts, and management of overburden and red-earth materials—all governed by Jamaican environmental permits, licenses, and mining lease conditions.

Key Responsibilities

Environmental Strategy & Leadership

Define and own the environmental strategy, policy, standards, permits, and related management systems that apply consistently across both operations while respecting each jurisdiction's legal requirements.
Establish a single, harmonized environmental management framework (aligned to ISO 14001 principles) that sets a common standard of performance while accommodating US and Jamaican regulatory differences.
Serve as the company's principal environmental authority, advising the executive team and Board on environmental risk, liabilities, obligations, capital requirements, and emerging regulatory developments.
Embed environmental accountability into operational decision-making, capital planning, and site leadership performance objectives.

Regulatory Compliance — Gramercy (United States)

Ensure full and continuous compliance with all applicable US federal and Louisiana state environmental requirements, including the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA), and Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act (EPCRA).
Own the site's Title V air operating permit, Louisiana water discharge (LPDES) permit, and all related permits, ensuring conditions, monitoring, and reporting obligations are met.
Maintain compliant relationships and correspondence with the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality (LDEQ) and applicable local agencies.
Oversee Toxic Release Inventory (TRI / Form R), Tier II, greenhouse gas, and other mandated federal and state reporting.
Direct Spill Prevention, Control and Countermeasure (SPCC), stormwater, and hazardous/industrial waste programs.
Optimize management of environmental liabilities and closure related plans.

Regulatory Compliance — St. Ann (Jamaica)

Ensure full compliance with Jamaican environmental and mining legislation, including the Natural Resources Conservation Authority (NRCA) Act, environmental permits and licenses, and conditions of the Mining Act and applicable Special Mining Leases.
Maintain effective working relationships with the National Environment and Planning Agency (NEPA), the Natural Resources Conservation Authority (NRCA), the Jamaica Bauxite Institute (JBI), Mines and Geology Division / Commissioner of Mines, and applicable local agencies.
Manage environmental permit and license applications, renewals, Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs), environmental permit conditions, and related matters for mine exploration, development and expansion.
Ensure compliance with mined-land reclamation, restoration, and post-mining land-use obligations under Jamaican law and lease commitments.

Bauxite Residue, Waste & Materials Management

Direct the safe management, processing, monitoring, and long-term stewardship of bauxite residue (red mud) storage areas at Gramercy, including structural integrity, seepage control, water balance, and closure planning.
Oversee management of overburden, red-earth, tailings, and process waste materials at St. Ann in line with permit conditions and reclamation plans.
Ensure hazardous, industrial, and general waste is characterized, stored, transported, and disposed of in compliance with applicable regulations at both sites.

Air, Water, Land & Biodiversity

Oversee air emissions monitoring, control, and dust management across refining from bauxite discharging through to final product loading (Gramercy) and mining/drying/shipping (St. Ann) activities.
Manage water resources, process water, wastewater, and stormwater programs, including discharge monitoring, groundwater and surface-water protection, and water quality reporting.
Lead progressive mined-land reclamation, revegetation, reforestation, and biodiversity protection programs at St. Ann, and land stewardship and site remediation at Gramercy.

Permitting, Monitoring & Reporting

Own the full lifecycle of environmental permits, licenses, and authorizations at both operations—applications, renewals, modifications, and condition tracking.
Ensure timely, accurate, and defensible environmental monitoring, recordkeeping, and regulatory reporting in both jurisdictions.
Maintain an audit-ready compliance calendar and documentation system spanning both sites.

Incident Management & Emergency Response

Establish and maintain environmental incident prevention, spill response, and emergency preparedness programs at both operations.
Lead environmental incident investigations, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and regulatory notification and follow-up.
Ensure emergency response plans meet US and Jamaican requirements and are regularly tested and updated.

Auditing, Assurance & Continuous Improvement

Implement a program of internal and third-party environmental audits, inspections, and self-assessments across both sites.
Track environmental performance against targets, identify improvement opportunities, and drive corrective and preventive actions to closure.
Benchmark performance and adopt industry-leading practices in alumina refining and bauxite mining environmental management.

Stakeholder, Community & Sustainability Engagement

Represent Atalco with regulators, government agencies, industry bodies, and communities in both Louisiana and Jamaica.
Support community relations, land-use, and social-license initiatives associated with mining and refining operations.
Advance Atalco's sustainability, ESG, and greenhouse-gas / decarbonization reporting and commitments.
